title: Evidence export
description: The workings behind one reading: the path that reached the answers `reading.json` states. Its shape moves with the reading — `schemaVersion` rises when a key is added, renamed or removed, and no consumer contract holds it still — and this schema is what stops the writer changing the shape without stating it.

schemaVersion.description: The version of this document's shape. It rises when a key is added, renamed or removed.

repository.description: The name of the directory the reading was pointed at.

commit.description: The revision the caller states for the tree that was read, empty where it states none. The reading opens no .git.

seed.description: The seed every null in the reading was drawn with. The repository, the commit and the seed are the run: a reader holding this file can repeat it.

unplaced.description: The share of observed evidence resolving to no subject.

elapsedMillis.description: How long the reading took. A fact about the machine rather than the repository: two runs of one unchanged tree differ on it and on nothing a reading reports.

linkage.description: What the `url` fields in this document are: permalinks into a hosted repository at a commit, or links opening the file in the reader's own editor.

edges.description: Pairs of topics that share words, with the words two topics were both read from.

scopes.description: Every scope the build compiles as a unit, each with its divergence from the whole repository, the chance figures beside it, and the topics accounting for the divergence. The scopes within chance are here too, which is what `reading.json` omits.

bits.description: The Jensen-Shannon divergence between this scope's distribution over subjects and the whole repository's, bounded at 1 bit by base-2 logarithms.

excess.description: `bits` minus `nullMedian` — negative where the scope diverges less than a chance scope of its size.

atLeastAsExtreme.description: How many chance resamples reached this scope's divergence or beat it.

concentratedInScope.description: Whether the scope writes the topic at a higher density than the repository does.

filesRead.description: Every file read, with the topic leading it and that topic's share of the file.

dominant.description: The topic leading the file, empty where nothing was read from it.

matches.description: Every published term a bundled vocabulary found in a declared name, admitted or removed — one entry per term and normalisation, each matched over the index narrowed to the terms the reference corpus says are the vocabulary's own. The removed entries are the half `reading.json` counts and never lists.

term.description: The run of words the repository wrote.

normalisation.description: What both sides were normalised to before they were compared.

outcome.description: REPORTED, or REFUSED_BY_BRANCH_RULE for a one-word term written without another concept from its publisher's branch. A term with no REPORTED entry at any normalisation is one of `reading.json`'s `matchesDiscardedByBranchRule`.

concepts.description: The concepts the term reaches, under the labels the publisher states. Each REPORTED entry's concepts appear as rows of `reading.json`'s `taxonomies[].concepts`.

setAside.description: The rows behind three of the counts `reading.json` states under `setAside`, carried whole rather than ranked and truncated.

wordsNoResourceCovers.description: Every word no bundled resource has an entry for, most-written first.

wordsBelowEveryThreshold.description: Every word whose margin a reference's own bar refused. The count matches `reading.json`'s `wordsBelowEveryThreshold`, and each row's `verdict` names which of the two rules removed it.

refusedBy.description: Every reference whose bar the word's margin did not clear, with the claim, the margin and the bar in bits. A claim above the bar beside a margin below it is the error rule.

wordsTheLanguageSupplies.description: Every word that cleared every bar and is English rather than a subject.

workings.description: The path that places: what the resources said about every word the reading offered, what a rule removed, and what nothing read at all.

rules.description: Every rule that can remove a topic, with its whole effect on this reading — so a reader can see whether a rule is taking anything out before looking for what.

stated.description: What the rule does, in words.

words.description: One row per word the reading offered, ordered by `carried`. `shareByTopic` is what the resources state about the word; `carried` is what the word contributed, and the two disagree because a word can be offered, recorded, and then contribute nothing.

writtenAsAName.description: Whether the repository ever declared something with the word, rather than only writing prose about something.

senseCoverage.description: The share of the word's senses some resource put a subject on.

removed.description: One row per rule and topic, with a handful of the phrases it happened in — the half a reader cannot reconstruct, because a topic absent from an answer was either never voted for or voted for and taken out, and only the reading knows which.

unread.description: Every run of words nothing placed, kept as a run, with which of the two ways it went unread.

reason.description: The first two are findings — a gap in the resources. A dependency's coordinates were never asked about, because what a dependency states is stated by the artefact it names rather than by its spelling.

vocabulary.description: Every ranked word with the whole of its verdict, so the funnel from the field to the signals is arguable row by row. The rows with verdict SIGNAL are `reading.json`'s `signals`; the counts under its `setAside` partition the rest.

claim.description: The weakest reference's claim in bits, signed by which side writes the word more densely.

margin.description: The same claim with the reference's own sampling error held against the word. The verdict rests on it.

timesChance.description: The margin as a multiple of its own reference's threshold, at whichever leaves the least room. Absent where no reference has a positive bar.

verdict.description: SIGNAL, or the one rule that removed the word.

witness.description: One word's testimony for a topic: occurrences and mass disagree and both are stated, because a word written five hundred times can carry almost no mass.

linkedQuotation.description: The phrase a word was read in, with the site as a path and a link of the kind `linkage` names.

sitedQuotation.description: The phrase a word was read in, with the site as `path:line` alone.

topicVotes.description: What the resources state about a word read one way, each vote naming the subject, its mass and the resource that cast it. What a resource states and never what the word contributed.
